Something in my aquarium keeps breaking things.
Snail shells, cracked open like eggs.
And at night, the camera picks up this sound.
So I made a list of suspects.
Suspect one. The eel. Too lazy.
Suspect two. The octopus. Smart, but no hard parts.
Suspect three. The pufferfish. Strong beak, but asleep every night.
Then, one night, the glass cracked.
I turned on the light. And there it was.
Ten centimeters long. A mantis shrimp.
It punches with two little clubs, at eighty kilometers an hour.
So fast, the water around them bursts into bubbles.
That's how it cracked the glass.
But here's the weirdest part. Its eyes have up to sixteen kinds of colour sensors. We have three.
So it must see the most colours on Earth, right?
Wrong. In tests, it's worse at telling colours apart than we are.
It doesn't need to see. It just needs to punch.
So I moved it into its own tank. With extra thick glass.
Last night, I heard a click.
